speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to determine the cause, have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or a sore throat recently? REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, and Viral_Serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC, CRP, and viral serology results are normal, which makes a typical viral etiology less likely. Given the specific combination of forearm blisters and mucosal ulcers, have you recently been exposed to someone with cold sores, or have you noticed any sensitivity to sunlight? REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_of_forearm_blisters

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Captopril-induced cutaneous and mucosal toxicity (manifesting as fixed drug eruption or bullous drug eruption).

This diagnosis is supported by your recent initiation of captopril, which can cause blistering skin lesions and painful oral/genital ulcers, even in the absence of viral symptoms or abnormal inflammatory markers. Please stop taking the medication immediately and follow up for confirmation and management.
